**Practical notebook.** Apply point-cloud, graph and scalar-grid constructions
while keeping the scientific question visible. <a href="../../downloads/topic-05-participant.ipynb" download="topic-05-participant.ipynb">Download the notebook</a>.

::: {.column-margin .study-note .insight}
**Relation to the spine.** This topic revisits stages 1 and 3. The teaching
examples used one convenient route; real stored data require a justified
representation, constructor and filtration.
:::

A valid persistence calculation begins before software is called. The stored
data must become a filtered object without discarding relationships that were
already meaningful. Coordinates, networks, images and meshes therefore need
different starting constructions. Converting all of them into point clouds
would introduce assumptions that the data did not require.

The first practical question is:

> What is actually stored, and which relationships are already meaningful?

| Stored data | Natural representation | Filtration value means |
|---|---|---|
| coordinates or distances | Rips, Čech or alpha complex | spatial or state-space proximity |
| weighted graph | filtered graph or clique complex | edge strength, cost or dissimilarity |
| image, volume or scalar grid | cubical complex | intensity, density, energy or another field value |
| supplied mesh or complex | filter the existing cells | a measured value attached to vertices or cells |

![Four stored data types lead to different filtered objects.](../../assets/topic05-data-routes.svg){fig-alt="Four teal panels show a point cloud becoming a proximity complex, a weighted graph being thresholded, a scalar image becoming a cubical complex and a supplied mesh retaining its incidences."}

The table is a method map, not an automatic selector. The metric, filtration
direction and treatment of higher-order relations still come from the
scientific question.

::: {.column-margin .study-note .insight}
**Static is a computational description.** The input may be one window from a
changing system, one state-space cloud or one network at a selected time. The
calculation is static because it receives one object, not because the
scientific system is stationary.
:::

### Coordinates and distances

A metric point cloud supports a proximity construction. Rips complexes need
only pairwise distances. Čech complexes retain a direct connection to unions
of balls, while alpha complexes use Euclidean geometry to reduce the number
of simplices. Alpha shapes were introduced precisely as a scale-dependent
description of the shape of a finite Euclidean point set
[@edelsbrunner1994alpha]. Witness complexes instead select landmarks and use
the remaining observations as witnesses, reducing the vertex set
[@desilva2004witness]. These routes encode related but not identical
assumptions.

Coordinates do not make Euclidean distance compulsory. Units, periodic
coordinates, feature scaling and mixed variable types can all change which
observations count as neighbours.

### Weighted graphs

A weighted graph already states which pairwise relations are admissible. It
can remain one-dimensional, in which case graph cycles cannot be filled, or
complete subgraphs can be filled to form a clique complex. The latter asserts
that pairwise compatibility is sufficient evidence for a higher-order
relation.

Petri and collaborators provide a concrete weighted-network example. They
filter functional brain correlation networks, retain representative
one-dimensional cycles and assemble them into homological scaffolds; their
Figure 6 contrasts the resulting placebo and psilocybin scaffolds
[@petri2014scaffolds]. The interpretation depends on both the edge weights and
the clique-based higher-order completion.

::: {.column-margin .study-note .audience-dynamics}
**Graph versus clique complex.** A triangular graph records three pairwise
relations. Its clique complex additionally treats the triple as one filled
relation. That choice can determine whether the visible cycle contributes to
homology.
:::

### Images, volumes and scalar grids

A cubical complex retains the rectangular adjacency already present in an
array. Pixels become filled squares and voxels become filled cubes. A sublevel
filtration reveals low values first; a superlevel filtration reveals high
values first. Robins, Wood and Sheppard model two- and three-dimensional
greyscale images as cubical complexes; Section 5 shows persistent homology
calculations on digital-image examples [@robins2011images].

![A scalar image and its cubical sublevel filtration.](../../assets/topic05-cubical-data-filtration.svg){fig-alt="The raw five-by-five image assigns value one to a ring, value five to its central pixel and value four outside. At threshold one the ring pixels enter but the value-five centre does not; at threshold five the centre enters and fills the hole."}

The missing centre is not drawn by hand. It is the pixel whose recorded value
is $5$. At threshold $a=1$, the eight value-$1$ pixels have entered while the
centre has not, so the included squares surround an absent square. At $a=5$,
that data value is admitted and the opening is filled. The feature is a
statement about the scalar values and sublevel direction, not merely the
rectangular grid.

The filtration coordinate now has the units of the scalar field. Reversing
the direction changes the question, for example from low-energy basins to
high-density regions.

### Existing meshes and complexes

If the data already include a mesh, cell complex or scientifically defined
interaction complex, retain it when possible. A value on vertices can be
extended to simplices by a lower-star rule, so each simplex enters no earlier
than its faces. The terrain example in the original persistence and
simplification paper demonstrates this route for a scalar function on an
existing triangulated domain [@edelsbrunner2002persistence]. Rebuilding the
object as an unrelated point cloud may erase the incidence structure supplied
by the data.

::: {.column-margin .study-note .qualification}
**Labels may also be structure.** Cell type, agent role or species can be part
of the observation rather than decoration. Chromatic persistence is one
specialist family of constructions that retains such labels instead of
discarding them before topology is computed [@cultrera2024chromatic].
:::

## Construction choice versus parameter choice

Replacing a graph by its clique complex, negating a scalar field or replacing
Euclidean distance by correlation changes the represented question. Changing
a numerical threshold within one documented construction explores scale
inside that question.

This distinction explains why applications use different routes. Grid-cell
population activity can be represented as a high-dimensional point cloud
[@gardner2022torus], amorphous structures as geometric point configurations
[@hiraoka2016hierarchical], and aggregation models as point clouds in
position-velocity space [@topaz2015aggregation]. Their shared algebra does not
make the represented objects interchangeable.

## Checkpoints

You are ready to continue when you can identify the stored data object,
select a representation without unnecessarily discarding structure, state
what the filtration value means, and distinguish a construction choice from a
parameter change within that construction.
